minutes.headline: Task force plans to bring a stormwater utility bylaw (not yet the fee) to May 2026 town meeting
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force met with its consultant (Weston and Sampson) to review contract progress on impervious surface data, rate structure, and public engagement materials, and spent most of the meeting building a detailed calendar of Finance Committee, Select Board and public information session dates leading up to the March 16 warrant closing and May town meeting. The group decided to bring forward only the enabling bylaw establishing the utility framework this spring, holding the fee/rate structure and budget vote for a later town meeting, and reviewed a draft stormwater budget with the DPW representative covering Chapter 90 and residential/commercial funding splits. No members of the public were present or commented, and the only votes taken were procedural approvals of prior minutes and adjournment.

what_happened.line: Task force will bring only a stormwater utility bylaw, not the fee, to the May 2026 town meeting.
A calendar of Finance Committee, Select Board and public sessions was set ahead of the March 16 warrant closing.
Members reviewed a draft stormwater budget with the DPW, including Chapter 90 funds and cost splits.
A member said fee revenue would largely replace an existing tax-funded stormwater line, not add a new cost outright.
One public information session is planned for March 5, with a second held in reserve for a fall town meeting.

why_it_matters: The May town meeting vote would create the legal framework for a stormwater utility; the fee and rate structure would come to a later town meeting, so this vote does not set anyone's bill.
The fee is planned to offset money the town already raises through taxes for stormwater work, so whether a resident's total bill rises depends on how much of that existing line is removed.
Residents can weigh in at the March 5 information session before the bylaw language goes to the March 16 warrant.
